title: Flow-Mapper harvest manifest
description: One service's harvested map. kind=full replaces the snapshot; kind=delta patches it against baseVersion.

id.description: Stable ID, unique within the service for its entity type.

bindKey.description: Opaque key produced by the harvester. Literal unless match=glob.

match.description: glob: * matches any characters except slash, ** matches anything. amqp-topic (a binding on a RabbitMQ topic exchange, `amqp:<exchange>/<binding key>`): * is exactly one dot-separated word, # is zero or more words.

transport.description: undecided: the transport of a call or endpoint in a design is not decided yet (the bind key still links the two ends; sync, unicast by default). Harvesters never send it.

delivery.description: unicast links to the most specific match; multicast to all matches. Defaults by transport.

eventType.description: Event type name as the harvester sees it (message type attribute, detail-type, class name). Matched exactly; 'OrderPlaced.v2' is not 'OrderPlaced'.

eventPattern.description: An event type, or a glob over event types: '*' for all, 'Order*' for a prefix.

eventFilter.description: Event types a subscription lets through. Absent means all. An entry starting with '!' excludes a type or glob (SNS anything-but / prefix exclusion): ["!revision.status"] is everything except that type; ["Order*", "!OrderDraft*"] is Order types except drafts.

source.description: Where the item is defined (code or IaC). commit and repo override the manifest's for this item's code link; set commit only when this item was scanned at a different commit.

provenance.description: Which harvester run produced the item, and whether it was checked against the live system.

via.description: Wrapper hops between the caller's call site and the real SDK call, in call order (the last hop is the one that calls the SDK). The call still counts once: hops are never producers, nodes or edges.

version.description: Resolved version, e.g. 5.3.2. Leave out (and send unresolved what=client) when unknown; never invent one.

versionSource.description: Where the version came from: lockfile, package.json, …

client.description: How a service reaches a data store (on a resource) or a non-store target (on an egress): its access mode, its own driver, and the wrapper library with the driver bundled in it. One client per client site; a service that reaches one store in two ways sends two resources.

accessId.description: Stable id of the client site, e.g. orders-svc/src/redis.ts:12.

databases.description: Redis: the database indexes this client selects (db0, db1…). Shown on the instance page next to the client.

lib.description: The wrapper library and the driver it bundles; null or omitted for direct_driver.

driver.description: The driver nested inside the library (it may differ from the service's own).

via.description: Wrapper hops from the caller to the SDK call, same shape as egress `via`.

callSite.description: One place in the service's code that makes this call, with the wrappers it goes through.

unresolved.description: What the harvester found but could not resolve, and why. what=target: the call target or consumed key (bindKey, or a step's target, may then be left out). what=event: the event type (candidates = the possible types). what=client (on a resource or egress): a field of its `client` the harvester could not resolve; `detail` names the field (e.g. driver.version or lib.driver.version), `reason` says why (e.g. lockfile_not_found). what=instance (on a resource): the collection is known (bindKey set) but the DB instance id is not yet; the resource keeps its bindKey and groups with the same collection's other users (schemas still attach); `detail` is the known text, e.g. p81/p81-production. what=detail (on a resource or a resource step): a value the harvester knows exists but could not read; `detail` is the field path, `reason` says why. Known paths: details.databases (on an instance resource), client.databases (on a service resource), details.keyTemplate, details.dbIndex, details.ttlSeconds (on a resource step). The UI shows it as "unknown (reason)", which reads differently from a field that is simply absent; it is never a broken link. what=caller (on a function): the backward walk stopped here because no caller could be resolved (reason e.g. unknown_receiver, callback_passed; candidates = possible callers, as function ids).

candidates.description: Possible bind keys (target) or event types (event).

assumed.description: Values you filled by a rule instead of reading them from code (the mirror of `unresolved`). Say what, the value used, what it rests on and why; readers show it as an assumed default, never as a fact. what: a first-class name (database, ttl, ...) or "detail" with `detail` = the field path, like unresolved (e.g. details.databases, client.databases, details.dbIndex, details.ttlSeconds). A field may not be both unresolved and assumed (contract finding assumed-and-unresolved). It changes nothing in the graph or in link resolution; health lists it apart from problems.

value.description: The value actually used; any JSON.

basis.description: Short code: client_default, convention, inferred_from_name, sibling_value; free text allowed.

reason.description: One sentence: which default or rule, and who approved it.

details.description: Free-form transport details (method, path, queue URL, timeouts, …).

links.description: Where to read more (0.25.1): one main link and up to 20 sub links. Shown by the UI; never part of linking or flows.

kind.description: client-app: a device or browser application (an agent, a mobile app) that calls services; it has no ingress of its own to harvest.

about.description: Optional (0.30.2). A rich description of the component in Markdown-lite (## headings, **bold**, *italic*, ~~strike~~, `code`, lists, [text](https://...) links; no HTML). By convention sections: ## Capabilities, ## Motivation, ## Roles and responsibilities, ## Owners, ## Open questions. Shown in the component panel; diffs like any header field.

owners.description: Optional (0.33.0). Who owns the component, as structured people (the free-text "## Owners" section of about stays allowed). Each owner is a name, or { name?, externalSource, externalId } (for example the Confluence account id); the server matches it to a user (external id first, then an exact name or alias) and creates the user when nothing matches. Stored and read back as a list of user ids. Left out: keeps what is there on a delta; [] clears.

groupPath.description: Optional. The subsystem the service belongs to, as a path: "platform", later "platform/identity". Harvesters may leave it out; design environments set it.

details.description: Free-form. `runtime`: k8s-pod | k8s-deployment | k8s-daemonset | k8s-operator | k8s-job. In a design (an HLD import): `doc` (file, section, quote, confidence) says where the component comes from.

target.description: Function id, egress id or resource id in this service.

altGroup.description: Steps of this function with the same altGroup are mutually exclusive alternatives, one branch per condition (drawn as an alt frame). Without it, consecutive steps with the same source file:line that each carry a condition form a group.

groups.description: The frames this step sits in, outermost first, so frames nest (an alt inside a loop). Each entry: `id` (unique within the function; steps sharing an id are in one frame), `kind` (alt, opt, loop, par, critical or break; default alt) and `condition` (the section of the frame this step is in; steps with the same condition share a section, none = the frame's only section). When present it replaces `altGroup` and `condition` for the grouping of this step.

mark.description: A step the design adds (new) or changes (changed): drawn as a coloured band on its arrow with the same mark icon as components and flows, and counted by "Changed only". `details.changed` (free text) stays the tooltip.

over.description: On a leaf step: the components (or data stores, by their instance or database name) its note spans. The note is drawn from the leftmost to the rightmost of them (one component: under that lifeline).

returns.description: What this call returns (#81). `label` (1 to 80 characters, one line of plain text) is drawn on the dashed return arrow of a sync call (without `returns` the arrow says "return"); `detail` (plain text, up to 500 characters) shows in the step panel and as the arrow's tooltip. A Mermaid `B-->>A: text` import sets the label.

event.description: For an egress step: the event type it publishes.

bind.description: For a call step: values handed to the callee, by name, e.g. {"event": "entry.does.not.exist"}. Visible to the callee and everything it calls on this path; the nearest bind of a name wins.

eventFrom.description: For an egress step: take the event type from the nearest enclosing call step's bind of this name on the traced path (a publish whose event type is a parameter of the function). Unbound on a path: treated as a publish that names no event.

source.description: Where the call is made: file, line, col. Shown as a code link on the trace message.

access.description: For a resource step: read, write or read_write (e.g. findOneAndUpdate; shown as R/W, counts as reader and writer). Default: from the operation name (find, GET, SELECT, GetItem… are reads).

fields.description: For a resource step: the fields of the stored object this call touches, names only, never values.

path.description: Field path, e.g. status or address.city.

inDdl.description: false: the code uses a field that is not in the collection's schema (flagged in the UI and the contract report).

ddlRef.description: Link to the schema/DTO field, e.g. Order.status.

details.description: Free-form step details. On a `resource` step of a Redis instance (#29): `keyTemplate` (the key template the call touches, e.g. session:{tenantId}:{userId}), optional `dbIndex` and `ttlSeconds` (the TTL this call sets). With keyTemplate, the instance page lists the flows that write the key.

origin.description: 'frontier': part of a call tree that reaches no sink. Traces fold frontier steps into one marker per function and do not count them toward maxMessages unless asked to expand them. Default 'path': as before.

kind.description: 'leaf': a step that ends the call tree and has no target (db_access, external_pkg…); say what it is in `operation` and `note`. A `call` step with no target but an `operation` or `note` is a leaf too. Not an unresolved gap.

commit.description: Only when this function was scanned at a different commit than the manifest's.

details.description: Free-form. In a design (an HLD import): `doc` says where the function comes from.

handler.description: Function id that handles this ingress.

middleware.description: Optional. Function ids (same manifest, same rule as `handler`) that run before the handler, in order. Traced before the handler: their calls are real messages and edges. `details.middleware` is still accepted (not traced).

entryPoint.description: true: always an entry point (public API, cron, a client's own trigger); excluded from orphan stats. false: never one (a hop such as a tunnel, BGP or BFD session that keeps its real transport). Absent: the default rule (a socket ingress, an RPC command, or an ingress nothing reaches is one).

details.description: Free-form. RabbitMQ RPC (0.18.0): on an ingress with bind key `amqp-rpc:{command}`, `rpc` {command, commandQueue, replyTo, exchange, correlation, timeoutMs, library, prefetch} (the server's side; what the caller declares is completed with it).

via.description: How the handler was resolved, for registrations that are not a direct reference: hops from the registration to the handler, each kind 'registration' or 'bind'. `details.handlerVia` is still accepted.

events.description: Event types this consumer handles, each with its own handler. The most specific match wins.

handler.description: Function id that handles this event type.

producers.description: Declared producer services, for producers Flow-Mapper does not harvest. Harvested producers are found automatically.

details.description: Free-form. RabbitMQ (0.18.0): on a publish, `exchange`, `routingKey` (placeholders such as {deviceId} count as one word) and, for a headers exchange, `headers`; on an RPC call (bind key `amqp-rpc:{command}`, mode sync), `rpc` {command, commandQueue, replyTo, exchange, correlation, timeoutMs, library}.

events.description: Event types published through this egress.

callSites.description: Every place that makes this call, each with its own `via`. `details.via` and `details.callSites` are still accepted.

bindKey.description: Shared key so services using the same store are grouped: {kind}:{cluster or db}/{collection, table or key pattern}, e.g. mongodb:orders-db/orders, redis:cache-main/order:{id}. The part before '/' groups keys of one cluster.

details.description: Free-form. Redis (#29): on a service's resource, `access` (read | write | read_write: what the service does through this connection; else derived from its steps) and the interim `keys` (top N key templates: [{keyTemplate, dbIndex, commands, access, opsPerHour, ttlSeconds}]) and `lazy` {kind: 'keys', ref}; on the infra resource that defines the instance (bindKey redis:<name>, no key pattern): `engineVersion`, `nodes`, `topology` (cluster | standalone), `databases`.
Free-form. RabbitMQ (0.18.0): on an `amqp-exchange`, `type` (topic | direct | fanout | headers), `vhost`, `durable`, `alternateExchange`; on an `amqp-queue`, `role` (rpc-command | rpc-reply).

from.description: Source channel key, or a pattern when match=glob.

details.description: Free-form. RabbitMQ (0.18.0): `bindingKey` (the key as written in code), and on a headers exchange `headers` and `xMatch` (all | any).
